subject: Distribution assumption of latent spatial field

messages.author: 78de4c49c6c78f17
messages.subject: Distribution assumption of latent spatial field
parts:
Dear INLA-Group,

for a M.Sc. research project  in statistics I am fitting a spde model to cosmic matter density field data. In order to catch the skewness of the data better I would like to change the distribution assumption of the latent field to a lognormal distribution,
like:

Is it possible to implement this with R-INLA?  Could I even implement a convolution of a gaussian and a log-gaussian latent field as underlying spatial process?

Thanks for your help!

Thanks for your answer! I am not exactly sure but I guess it should be 

Y ~ exp(intercept + spde) 

as the observable should be explained only by the spatial process.

I defined the effects in the inla.stack function as

effects = list(mesh.index, intercept = rep(1, n_loc*n_maps))

And the formula as

Y ~ -1 + intercept + f(field, model = spde,  group = field.group,  control.group = list(model = „iiid“))

I have tried to change the link via control.link in the inla function but I 

Receive the error message that control.ink argument is not used.


Where can I change the link-function in order to get a lognormal distributed latent field?


Regards,

Amelie Liese

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Distribution assumption of latent spatial field
parts:
Hi,

I have implemented the code with the exp() link function in order to model a latent logGaussian-field. 

cmp <- ~ -1  + Intercept(1) + field(coordinates, model = spde)

form <- obs ~ exp(Intercept + field)

fit <- bru(components = cmp,
           like(formula = form, data = df, family = "lognormal"),
           options = list(inla.mode = "experimental",
                          control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb"))
)

It would be great if someone could give me a short feedback wether this is the correct implementation.

Kind regards,

Amelie

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Distribution assumption of latent spatial field
parts:
Hi,
No, the lognormal observation model already applies a log-link by default (i.e. an exponential transformation of the linear predictor), so you just need to use
form = obs ~ Intercept + field
See inla.doc(“lognormal”).

It’s only when using predict() on the result that you need to specify the whole expression; at that stage it does not automatically apply the transformation, so there you will need ~exp(Intercept + field)

Finn
